skills.name: architect
skills.description: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.

skills.name: arena
skills.description: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.

skills.name: automate-me
skills.description: Turn a demonstrated repeated workflow into a reusable Rakazo skill or an explicitly requested native schedule.

skills.name: benchmark-checklist
skills.description: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured.

skills.name: blast-radius
skills.description: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust.

skills.name: bro
skills.description: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.

skills.name: comment-sicko
skills.description: Review scoped comments and suppressions for redundancy or hidden design problems; return evidence-backed deletion and refactoring suggestions.

skills.name: correct
skills.description: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and write docs last. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Repeat this each time the operator corrects you. Use for /correct.

skills.name: create-formal-verification-skill
skills.description: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, "model-check this race", "prove this invariant", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests.

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.

skills.name: figure-it-out
skills.description: Design an auditable playbook when no narrower one fits: a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, or work a human reviews after stepping away. Scales rigor to the task, runs a hypothesis loop, and logs decisions. Use for /figure-it-out or 'figure it out'.

skills.name: how
skills.description: Use for "how does X work", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions ("where should this live", "which package owns this", "is this the right layer"). Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation.

skills.name: in-your-own-words
skills.description: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve. Use for /in-your-own-words.

skills.name: ketchup
skills.description: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, in plain words and small visuals. List every item waiting on them with what they need to decide it from the reply alone. Use for /ketchup.

skills.name: ketchup-video
skills.description: Catch the user up like /ketchup, with a short subtitled video of slides for what happened and the waiting calls as text under it. Use for /ketchup-video.

skills.name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
skills.description: Bring a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes: find the commits that touched verified code, update the model, harness, or properties to describe the code as it is now, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, "is the model still true to the code", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it.

skills.name: maintain-verification-skill
skills.description: Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or "audit the verify skill".

skills.name: make-bot-ui
skills.description: Build a scoped UI that sends authenticated events to a Rakazo bot through its native webhook.

skills.name: no-comments
skills.description: Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.

skills.name: principle-attack-the-premise
skills.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

skills.name: principle-boundary-discipline
skills.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

skills.name: principle-build-the-lever
skills.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

skills.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
skills.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

skills.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
skills.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

skills.name: principle-experience-first
skills.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

skills.name: principle-explain-the-number
skills.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

skills.name: principle-fix-root-causes
skills.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

skills.name: principle-foundational-thinking
skills.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

skills.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
skills.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

skills.name: principle-laziness-protocol
skills.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

skills.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
skills.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

skills.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
skills.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

skills.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
skills.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

skills.name: principle-model-the-domain
skills.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

skills.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
skills.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

skills.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
skills.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

skills.name: principle-prove-it-works
skills.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

skills.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
skills.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

skills.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
skills.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

skills.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
skills.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

skills.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
skills.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

skills.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
skills.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

skills.name: principle-type-system-discipline
skills.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

skills.name: recall
skills.description: Reconstruct a scoped working context from Rakazo chat history, connected records and current evidence.

skills.name: reflect
skills.description: Review the current Rakazo conversation for durable lessons and propose or apply specifically authorized skill improvements.

skills.name: reproduce-and-fix-issues
skills.description: Reproduce triaged Slack bugs through a configured app-control adapter, verify existing fixes, and open a bounded draft pull request only after before-and-after proof. Use only from the configured Benny repro automation.

skills.name: rstack
skills.description: Rakazo-native engineering workflows: start a coding, debugging, investigation or review task; use rstack-help to browse the full package.

skills.name: rstack-agent
skills.description: Helper role for a bounded implementation or evidence task delegated during a rstack workflow.

skills.name: rstack-help
skills.description: Browse the full rstack package and choose a workflow or principle for a concrete Rakazo task.

skills.name: rstack-interrogate
skills.description: Use for "rstack-interrogate", "adversarial review", "multi-model review", "challenge this", "stress test this code", "find blind spots", or "tear this apart". Adversaries try to break a change or design, and only findings proven by a run survive.

skills.name: rstack-mode
skills.description: Select and run the appropriate rstack engineering workflow in Rakazo, with native helpers and verifiable completion.

skills.name: setup-benny
skills.description: Prepare optional Benny issue-triage and reproduction recipes for Rakazo; create live jobs only when explicitly requested.

skills.name: setup-rstack
skills.description: Check that rstack skills and required Rakazo tools are available; configure only user-requested workflow preferences.

skills.name: sharpen
skills.description: Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt. Use for /sharpen.

skills.name: show-me-your-work
skills.description: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). Local by default; commit it when a reviewer needs the trail to trust the result. Use for /show-me-your-work, autonomous or multi-phase runs, or work a human reviews after stepping away.

skills.name: statechart
skills.description: Check a TLA+ model of a system that moves between states, such as a product flow, a protocol, or a service, and draw it as a Mermaid statechart. The report gives the shortest path to each state that breaks a rule. Use for /statechart, or to show a bug as a path through states.

skills.name: swarm
skills.description: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets, and exploration.

skills.name: tdd
skills.description: Use only when the user explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test, OR when the bug has an obvious cheap local test target. Skip when the test path is unclear, expensive, integration-heavy, or not requested.

skills.name: teach
skills.description: Explain a body of work plainly so a person actually understands it. Runs the `how` and `why` skills and weaves what they find into one clear explanation. Use for 'teach me this', 'help me really understand X', 'explain this change or subsystem to me'.

skills.name: technical-writing
skills.description: Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax. Use for /technical-writing or when writing or reviewing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages.

skills.name: triage-issue-reports
skills.description: Triage Slack issue reports with one thread-only verdict, evidence review, cause-aware routing, tracker dedupe, and fail-closed ticket creation. Use only from the configured Benny triage automation.

skills.name: typescript-best-practices
skills.description: TypeScript best practices. Use when reading or editing any .ts or .tsx file.

skills.name: unslop
skills.description: Cut AI tells from any writing.

skills.name: why
skills.description: Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why we picked Y', design rationale, regressions, postmortems, or data-backed thresholds. Discovers available MCPs and queries each evidence category (source control, issue tracker, long-form docs, real-time chat, infrastructure observability, error tracking, product analytics warehouse) in parallel, then returns a cited read on decisions and tradeoffs. Use how for runtime behavior.
